messages.content:
The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(N=2100\). For each prime \(p\), track the \(p\)-adic exponent on each number.

A move replacing \(a,b\) by \(\gcd(a,b),\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\) changes the exponent pair for each prime from \((x,y)\) to \((\min(x,y),\max(x,y))\). Thus, for every prime \(p\), the multiset of \(p\)-exponents on the board is invariant.

When Mark stops, no move changes the board. For two positive integers \(x,y\),

\[
\{\gcd(x,y),\operatorname{lcm}(x,y)\}=\{x,y\}
\]

holds exactly when one of \(x,y\) divides the other. Hence the final numbers form a divisibility chain. Sorting them as

\[
x_1 \le x_2 \le \cdots \le x_{2100}
\]

we have \(x_i \mid x_{i+1}\), so for every prime \(p\), the exponents \(v_p(x_i)\) are nondecreasing. Since the multiset of exponents is invariant, \(v_p(x_i)\) must be the \(i\)-th smallest \(p\)-exponent among the original numbers \(1,2,\dots,2100\).

We need \(x_{2026}\). The number of original integers with \(p\)-exponent at least \(k\) is

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^k} \right\rfloor.
\]

The \(2026\)-th smallest exponent is the largest \(k\) such that at least

\[
2100-2026+1=75
\]

original numbers have exponent at least \(k\). Thus

\[
e_p=v_p(x_{2026})=\max\left\{k:\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^k}\right\rfloor\ge 75\right\}.
\]

Since \(2100=75\cdot 28\), this is equivalent to

\[
e_p=\max\{k:p^k\le 28\}.
\]

Now compute:

\[
\begin{aligned}
2^4=16\le 28<32 &\implies e_2=4,\\
3^3=27\le 28<81 &\implies e_3=3,\\
5^2=25\le 28<125 &\implies e_5=2,\\
7,11,13,17,19,23 &\implies e_p=1.
\end{aligned}
\]

All other primes have exponent \(0\). Therefore

\[
x_{2026}=2^4\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23.
\]

The number of positive divisors is

\[
(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6
=5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 64
=3840.
\]

\[
\boxed{3840}
\]
